Crude through plain pipe is the cheapest option. Pipe-to-ground costs more iron (2 pieces = 10 pipe + 5 iron and cover 11 tiles, about 15 iron, against 11 iron for 11 plain pipes). It's only worth using where you cross something, and this route crosses nothing. Barrels cost even more.

Factorio 2.0 caps a fluid segment at a 320-tile extent, and the route is about 400 tiles. So put one pump in the middle at the coal-field poles, which splits the line into about 180 + 222 tiles.

A gear assembler and a pipe assembler, fed from the y=-25.5 iron belt, supply gears and pipes to all three engine inputs. Steel, copper and circuits stay hand-filled.

**Before you build:**
- **12 tiles by hand.** Most of the ghosts can't go on tiles where chests still stand. For each tile in the table, pick up the chest and place the item shown. Move what's inside first: circuits go to the new circuit chests, steel to the new steel chests.

| Tile | Place | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| (13.5,-52.5) | belt, east | plastic output |
| (0.5,-52.5) | belt, south | sulfur output |
| (-4.5,-66.5), (3.5,-66.5), (11.5,-66.5) | belt, north | old sulfur chests |
| (-4.5,-70.5), (3.5,-70.5), (11.5,-70.5) | belt, north | old circuit-and-plastic chests |
| (11.5,-62.5) | belt, west | old engine chest |
| (3.5,-62.5), (-4.5,-62.5) | underground-belt exit, west | old engine chests; they pair with the entrances at (8.5,-62.5) and (0.5,-62.5) |
| (24.5,-26) | splitter, west | a ghost is already there; if it doesn't build over the existing belt, pick up the belt and place it by hand |

- **Underground belts:** you need 12 in total and have about 10 left after the coal line. Craft one more pair (10 iron + 5 belts).
- **The iron belt:** check that y=-25.5 really carries iron. If one lane carries something else, that lane will just stop in the branch and the iron lane still flows. If both lanes are mixed, the branch will jam.

**(a) Plastic and sulfur** (122 belts, 4 underground belts, 2 splitters, 3 iron chests, 3 inserters, 3 small poles)

- **Sulfur:** from (0.5,-52.5) it turns east at (0.5,-51.5) and runs along y=-51.5 to x=19.5.
  - Underground at x 6.5→8.5, under the crude pipe at x 7.5.
  - Underground at x 11.5→13.5, under the coal belt at x 12.5.
  - At (19.5,-51.5) it turns north, then west at (19.5,-52.5), and joins the trunk from the east.
- **Plastic:** from (13.5,-52.5) it runs east along y=-52.5 to x=17.5 and joins the trunk from the west.
- **Lanes:** because the two belts join the trunk from opposite sides, plastic gets one lane and sulfur the other. Neither can block the other.
- **Trunk:** starts at (18.5,-52.5) and runs north up x=18.5 to y=-76.5. It doesn't touch the gas header, which ends at x=11.5. Then it runs west along y=-76.5.
- **Splitters:** at (11.5,-77) and (3.5,-77), both facing west, with the top run on y=-77.5.
  - Down-belts run south on x=10.5, x=2.5 and x=-5.5, the last fed from the end of the top run.
  - At y=-65.5 each one turns east, then north up its column's input line at x=11.5, 3.5 and -4.5.
- **What each column's input line does:**
  - It passes (x,-66.5), where the existing inserter takes sulfur for the chem-science assembler.
  - It ends at (x,-70.5), where the existing inserter takes plastic for the advanced-circuit assembler.
- **Circuits move** to new chests on the east side at (1.5 / 9.5 / 17.5, -70.5). Each has an inserter at (0.5 / 8.5 / 16.5, -70.5) facing east, and a new pole at (0.5 / 8.5 / 16.5, -72.5).

**(b) Gear and pipe feed** (48 belts, 8 underground belts, 1 splitter, 2 assembling-machine-1, 7 inserters, 2 small poles, 3 iron chests)

- **Iron:** a splitter at (24.5,-26) on the y=-25.5 belt sends iron up x=23.5. It goes underground at y -42.5→-44.5 to cross the y=-43.5 lab-feed belt and ends at (23.5,-63.5). Once the branch fills, all the iron goes back to the depot.
- **Assemblers:** gears at (20.5,-63.5) and pipes at (20.5,-57.5). Each takes iron through an inserter at x=22.5 facing east.
- **Outputs:** both drop onto a belt at (20.5,-60.5) heading west.
  - The gear inserter at (20.5,-61.5) faces north and the pipe inserter at (20.5,-59.5) faces south.
  - Because they drop from opposite sides, gears get one lane and pipes the other, so it can't jam.
- **Route to the engine assemblers:**
  - Along y=-60.5: underground from x=19.5 to 17.5, under the trunk.
  - Up x=11.5 to the column-3 engine tile (11.5,-62.5).
  - Underground from x=8.5 to the column-2 engine tile (3.5,-62.5).
  - Underground from x=0.5 to the column-1 engine tile (-4.5,-62.5), where it ends.
  - The engine assemblers' existing inserters pick gears and pipes off this belt.
- **Steel:** new chests at (-4.5 / 3.5 / 11.5, -63.5), each with an inserter at (-3.5 / 4.5 / 12.5, -63.5) facing west.
- **Power:** poles at (21.5,-61.5) and (21.5,-55.5). They link to the pole at (16.5,-64.5).

**Supplies you can tap:**
- **Iron:** only y=-25.5, now tapped. The y=-43.5 belt is the lab feed, so leave it alone.
- **Copper:** nothing on a belt near here. The plates go east to claude-1's red science at (50.5,-16.5). The block needs about 22 copper/min (0.375/s), so keep hand-filling the cable chests at (x,-74.5). One full chest lasts about 3.5 hours per column.
- **Circuits:** this is the real bottleneck. The base makes 25/min and uses 18/min, but the block needs about 22/min. Stamp a second gear-circuit block, which makes 40/min. It could hang off this same iron branch plus a copper source.
- **Steel:** nothing automated. claude-2's steel column at (53,30) could be belted to the steel chests later. For now, hand-fill about 150 steel per column per hour.
